notes: Empty list: ZeroDivisionError (naive), 0.0 (lenient), StatisticsError (statistics.mean), nan (missing-aware / running), or ValueError (strict).
None / NaN elements: propagate or TypeError (naive, strict, running), skipped as missing values (missing-aware), or rejected explicitly (strict).
Numeric strings like '1': coerced via float() (lenient) vs TypeError everywhere else.
Booleans: counted as 0/1 by most candidates, rejected with TypeError by the strict one.
Overflow on huge values ([1e308, 1e308]): naive sum gives inf, math.fsum raises OverflowError, exact-rational statistics.mean and incremental mean return 1e308.
Floating-point precision: naive sum/len vs fsum vs exact rational vs incremental update can differ in the last bits (e.g. ten 0.1s).

Summation precision: naive left-to-right sum, math.fsum, exact rational (Fraction) mean, and Welford running mean round differently on [0.1,0.2,0.3] (0.20000000000000004 vs 0.19999999999999998 vs 0.2) and on [1e16,1.0,-1e16] (0.0 vs 0.3333333333333333).

Overflow: [1e308,1e308] gives inf (naive), OverflowError (fsum), or the true value 1e308 (exact/running mean); the running mean itself degrades to nan on [1e308,-1e308,1e308] because intermediate differences overflow.
None as missing data: one candidate silently skips None (so [1,None,3] -> 2.0 and [None,None] -> ValueError like empty); all others raise TypeError.
Numeric strings: the float()-coercing candidate accepts ["1","2","3"] -> 2.0 and raises ValueError on "abc"; others raise TypeError for any string.
Result type: the exact candidate always returns float via float(); others rely on true division (still float for int/bool input).
